reply_text:
㊢ ("README-hardening.md in futon0") There's no `README-hardening.md` in futon0, and nothing by that name appears anywhere in its git history. The hardening material is spread across four files:
- `README-firewall.md`: the mesh firewall design from 08-13, which says it's design only and not implemented
- `README-secrets.md`: keys and access, from 08-17
- `README-bare-metal.md`: setup plus the disk-scan instructions added after the outage
- `~/README-ZONE-1.1.md` on zone: the post-rebuild state (ufw, keys-only SSH, parked timers)

I've corrected the pointer in the mission (`17b7dcc`), so the metameso recall gap now points to these files.

🈸 (if useful later) When hardening becomes a priority, a short `README-hardening.md` index over these four files, plus the open items from the outage (temperature/write monitoring, password sync, backups, metameso recall), would give it the single home you were remembering. I'll leave that alone unless you ask.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-13
previous_reply_acts.text:
("a virtual startup on Metameso and one on Lucy") I like that as a way to play with these ideas. I've written it down as an experiment shape. Each box would run one simulated venture with its own inner loop, for example a Saba-style purchasing co-op on one and a different dream on the other. Both would check in with zone, which acts as the co-op of co-ops. That exercises three things from today:
- cross-host recall, the gap we just deferred
- the outer loop's maintenance and compliance duties, which is where real co-ops fail
- a dry run of the "does FUTON help a non-technical dream?" test before a real person tries it
